_comment: Sharp Score v1 — see src/sharp/score.py and docs/intel/SHARP_SCORE.md. Weights are PRIORS chosen for defensibility, not values validated against an outcome dataset. Change them here, never in code; methodologyVersion must move with any change.

eligibility._comment: Hard gates. A manager failing ANY of these is 'evaluable: false' and is never scored, rather than being scored badly. Prevents thin-history managers from occupying the cohort.

weights._comment: Must sum to 1.0 across the positive components. uncertaintyPenalty is subtracted separately and is NOT part of that sum.

performance._comment: All inputs are percentile-normalized within the observed population before weighting, so no single raw stat can dominate and scales stay comparable across league sizes.

championshipShrinkage._comment: Championships are rare and high-variance: one title in one season is mostly luck. Beta-binomial shrink toward the population base rate with priorN pseudo-seasons.

rosterQuality._comment: Roster value is measured RELATIVE to each league's own average, so a manager in a shallow league cannot look sharp on raw value alone. Age adjustment prevents an old win-now roster from reading as dynasty strength.

multiLeagueConsistency._comment: The core anti-luck signal: repeated success across INDEPENDENT leagues is far harder to fake than one good run. Scored as the fraction of a manager's leagues where they finish above median, then penalized for variance across those leagues.

longevity._comment: Saturating: seasons 1->3 matter far more than 8->10.

activity._comment: Sustained participation, NOT raw transaction volume — churn is not skill. Capped so a hyperactive manager cannot buy their way into the cohort.

uncertaintyPenalty._comment: Subtracted from the weighted score. Scales with how far the manager's evidence falls short of a full record, so a 2-season manager cannot tie a 6-season manager on equal rates.

qualification._comment: A manager joins the cohort only by clearing BOTH the score bar and the confidence bar. Percentile is computed within the evaluable population, so the bar tightens automatically as coverage grows.

confidence._comment: Reported separately from the score, never blended into it. 'How much evidence' is a different question from 'how good'.
